evidence.detail: rs/g/a/a directly extends java.awt.event.KeyListener, so keyPressed, keyReleased and keyTyped are part of its exact JVM contract rather than inferred behavior.
The only central registry stores CopyOnWriteArrayList<rs/g/a/a>, and its registration/unregistration plus every dispatch loop are typed to this exact interface.
Exact v308 plugin/input classes including rs/l/f/j, rs/s/c/b and rs/s/j/b implement this interface and are dynamically registered by their owning live subsystems.

The interface adds one default boolean method returning false beyond the standard AWT KeyListener contract. R175 preserves the class-level listener role without inventing a narrower meaning for that extra hook.

candidates.note: ClientKeyListener is descriptive exact-behavior recovery for the AWT KeyListener extension registered by the client key-listener manager. The extra default hook remains intentionally unnamed. Confidence is 0.999.

evidence.detail: rs/g/a/b owns a CopyOnWriteArrayList<rs/g/a/a> with explicit add/remove methods and surviving log messages 'Registering key listener: {}' and 'Unregistered key listener: {}'.

Separate methods dispatch KeyEvent keyPressed, keyReleased and keyTyped to registered ClientKeyListener instances, with surviving trace strings 'Processing key pressed/released/typed ... for key listener {}'.

Each dispatch returns immediately if the incoming KeyEvent is already consumed; after invoking a listener it stops iteration when that listener consumes the event, with exact 'Consuming key ...' debug messages.

The base client rs/C forwards its AWT keyPressed, keyReleased and keyTyped events to this manager through Launcher/UI before legacy Client key handling; keyPressed and keyTyped return early when the manager path consumes the event.

Live overlay/plugin systems register and unregister ClientKeyListener implementations at lifecycle boundaries, including developer-tools and other client-side modules, establishing the manager as shared runtime input infrastructure rather than one feature-specific handler.

candidates.note: KeyListenerManager is fixed by its CopyOnWrite listener registry, three KeyEvent dispatch paths, consumption semantics and base-client front-gate integration. Confidence is 0.999.
